sources.entry: Quassel IRC - Distributed IRC client, meaning that one (or multiple) client(s) can attach to and detach from a central core. (Source Code) GPL-2.0 C++

summary.one_liner: Quassel IRC is a cross-platform, distributed IRC client whose core stays attached to IRC servers so one or more graphical clients can connect and disconnect.
summary.what_it_does: Quassel runs as a central core that keeps IRC connections open while clients attach and detach, similar to running screen with a text IRC client but with a graphical interface. The core handles storage through a database that is set up on first run via a connecting client's wizard, which also creates an admin user. The core command-line tool can add users, change user passwords, and accept a custom config directory. The README describes the project as free under the GPL and available on major platforms, with official stable downloads, nightly-style automated builds for Windows and macOS, and community-contributed builds. Development discussion happens on IRC (Libera Chat #quassel) and by email, and pull requests are accepted on GitHub while issues go to a separate bugtracker.
use_cases: keep IRC connections alive while away from the computer
chat on IRC from multiple devices with one shared session
self-hosted IRC bouncer with a graphical client
manage multiple IRC user accounts on a server
how_to_run: Start the Quassel core (quasselcore) and connect with a Quassel client; the first-run wizard creates the database and admin user
notable: Distributed design: a core stays connected while one or more clients attach and detach
Graphical client comparable to running screen with a text IRC client like WeeChat
First-run setup wizard creates the core database and an admin user
Free software under GPL, with builds for major platforms
caveats: README does not state a specific list of supported platforms beyond 'major platforms'
Windows and macOS automated builds are described as untested
GitHub issues are not used for bug reports; the separate bugtracker is used instead
